utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Aditya Menon, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson representing the Defence of General Delic; Lana Deljkic and Asja Zujo, our legal assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning to you, too, Witness PW-2. You may be aware of this, but it is my duty to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you took at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask the witness be shown Exhibit 79.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, PW-2, let me ask you if you are familiar with the Silver Shield award.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, PW-2, during the course of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, were you ever personally awarded the Silver Shield award?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, the document in front of you, Exhibit 79?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would ask we go into private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness PW-2, when you say that there were quite a few casualties, can you give us an approximate number, if you're able to do so, of the number of members of the El Mujahedin Detachment killed during the time period you were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know the figure. I can't really give you a figure, but I know that there were quite a few of them. Quite a few people were killed. People got killed in every action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, the document that's currently in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise or do you know the person listed on this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know Sulejman from Bugojno, but I can't recognise the last name. I don't know the last name, so I can't really tell you whether this is this person whom I knew or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page in both the B/C/S and the English versions of this document, please. Actually, it would be page 3 in English. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, do you recognise the name on the document that's currently -- or the page that's currently in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, how do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him from the El Mujahid Detachment, Adil Bosnic. I know him. He's deceased. He got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page, page 3, in the B/C/S version and page 5 of the English language version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, do you recognise or do you know the individual whose name appears on this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Edin, although I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, sir, how do you know this person that you've identified as "Edin"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would ask that the document P02610 be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document P026 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Document P02610 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 112.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown P02791, P02791, and we would ask that the witness be shown page 3 of this document in Bosnian and page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see this document in front of you, PW-2?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know the person whose name is listed on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do know Elvedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, PW-2, how do you know this person, Elvedin?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that this document, P02791, be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That document, P02791, is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 113.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, the last paragraph of that certificate appears to be calling for some explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I can ask the witness some questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If he knows, I would be interested. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, are you familiar or do you know the circumstances under which this person that you've identified as Elvedin was killed?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went home on a leave of absence. That's in Donji Vakuf. And I don't know the exact circumstances, but I know that he was killed by UNPROFOR troops in front of his home. He was not armed. He was with his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, I know you say you don't know the circumstances, but did you hear about this incident at the time or shortly thereafter; that is, in late 1995? Did you hear about what happened to this person Elvedin?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he was there. I don't know how this came about, so I can't make any claims about it. I just know that he was killed in front of his family house. I can't give you any more details. I don't know what the UNPROFOR troops thought and what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, PW-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness now be shown what was previously marked P01004. That's P01004. In the Bosnian language, that would be page 96; in the English language, that would be page 98, please. Again, I would ask that we go into private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, do you see a photo board in front of you with military insignia on it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps if we could just take the actual photo board and enlarge that for the benefit of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you if you recognise any of these military insignia that are depicted on P06187; and if you see any that you personally wore during the course of your service in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, if you could please give us the number which is contained in the upper right corner of each box on this photo board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The Prosecutor is already suggesting that all the emblems were worn in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If he did wear in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, he has to mention when and where he wore the insignia; otherwise, this is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you recognise any of these insignia that you personally wore, please, first of all, identify it, and then I'll ask you some follow-on questions.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there, sir. At what time period -- first of all, did you personally wear number 1; and if so, during what time period?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did wear it, yes, and this was in the period when I joined the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the other insignia as being those that you wore at any point in time when you served in the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. In the English interpretation had said "in the period when I joined the Muslim Forces," do we equate that with the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm simply asking him whether he -- which ones he wore at which time periods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I recognise number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness PW-2, can you tell the Trial Chamber what insignia's depicted in number 7 and at what time period or periods you wore that insignia?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I wore them, but it's familiar to me. I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is the insignia in Box 7 on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure whether those were the insignia of the Muslim Forces, "Muslimanske Snage," or of the 7th Muslim Brigade, but I remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise, sir, any of the other insignia as being insignia that you might have worn during the time period you were in the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible I wore number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At what time period, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but this is the insignia of the 7th Muslim Brigade, so I assume that I did wear it when I was a member of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise any other insignia that you wore at any point in time when you served in the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot see any others. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, PW-2. We'd ask that P06187 be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P06187 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 116.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, Witness PW-2, towards the end of the war, were you aware that there were any disbandment or farewell ceremonies for members of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a kind of farewell gathering in the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the approximate time period or date or month and year in which this farewell gathering occurred in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the war. I don't know exactly. Maybe the war was already over. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-2, where in Zenica this gathering occurred?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. In some meeting hall. I really don't know. I wasn't that familiar with the town at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you attend this gathering, PW-2?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there for a brief period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, which leaders of the El Mujahedin Detachment were present at this gathering?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the leaders were, but I know that there were foreign fighters there. Probably there were people from the Command, and we Bosniaks were also there. There were many people in that hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, sir, were there any leaders of the BH Army present on that occasion, senior leaders of the BH Army present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that some were present, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which senior leaders of the BH Army were present at this gathering in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically, but I think that there were people from the 3rd Corps, and I think that Mr. Delic was there. It was crowded. I cannot be 100 per cent certain, but there were senior officers there in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall, sir, when you say "there were people from the 3rd Corps," do you remember the identities or the names of any of the people from the 3rd Corps that were present?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty who was there. That wasn't absolutely something that I was interested in. I was there because I was invited. We were all invited.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall, sir, what took place at this farewell gathering in Zenica at the end of the war? What happened there?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that someone said that the war was over, that the foreign fighters had to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that there was even some kind of accord or agreement. I can't remember specifically, but I know that this was discussed, and that everyone has to leave Bosnia upon the signing of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-2, who it was that made these comments at that gathering?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, PW-2. The Prosecution has no further questions at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I move to questions, I would just like to move to private session first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] [Journalist]: "The actual exodus of Bosniaks living in the region of Bosanska Krajina started already in March 1992 with the arrival of the large formations of the former Yugoslav Army to this part of our country, as well as with the activation of Chetnik units made up of local people. "The crossing of Vlasic and the arrival of the ... citizens of Banja Luka, Prijedor, Sanski Most, Krupa, and other towns in Bosanska Krajina, meant an end to abuse and a transition into a somewhat more normal life. "Unfortunately, many people were not fortunate to cross Vlasic, because the Chetniks took them out of convoys and killed them, throwing into the canyon of river Ugar. "The two-month old Roko, from the village Vecica near Kotor Vators, was not so lucky to make it to Travnik. He died on the bus from thirst and exhaustion, and his mother would not let him out of her arms, even two days after his arrival in Travnik. Many met a similar fate. "Unfortunately, all of those who took the Vlasic road and crossed over to the free territory had know idea that their suffering was not completely over. The buildings housing the refugees were among those hit during the constant shelling of Travnik, and some people were killed and a considerable number were wounded. The scenes which were filled in July of last year when shrapnel from a tank grenade massacred the people located in a gymnasium are not for those with weak nerves. We are showing them for the first time. They speak for themselves, and thus any commentary would be superfluous. However, in spite of these excess situations, a river of refugees was flowing into Travnik almost daily. "This is what Semin Konjalic, the Commander of the District Staff of Civilian Protection in Travnik, has to say about all this." [Semin Konjalic]: "Just for your information, I will mention that, up until now, Travnik has received around 186.000 refugees. Currently, between 27 and 28.000 are present in our area. When we say that we managed in any way we could, you know that Travnik does not have any capacity to receive refugees. However, we used some of the collective centres such as the gymnasium and others. People there are not living in good conditions, but most of the refugees who came to our area have been accommodated, some adequately and some inadequately, but I hope that we will find better solutions in a better future. However, I have said that, from a geographic and strategical point of view, Travnik is in a bad location, because refugees are constantly pouring into this town; and, lately, we have been in a very difficult, unenviable condition regarding the accommodation and food, since, as you know, there is less and less food and more and more refugees." [Journalist]: "Unfortunately, the ethnic cleansing of the region of Bosanska Krajina continues in a systematic way, thus a large number of new refugees have continued to arrive, and this is how their reception has been organised." [Semin Konjalic]: "Let me tell you, as far as the new refugees are concerned, the arrival of around 5.000 of them from the Serb, the so-called Serb Krajina, has been announced."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to this interview, I would like to ask you the following: It's correct, isn't it, that in the events in the summer and fall of 1992, hundreds of thousands of refugees came to the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you agree that this caused a terrible situation in the region of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you something else. Please, you said that you volunteered to go to Bosnia as a volunteer?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you applied at the collection centre in Zagreb, the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This centre was in the area where the Zagreb Fair is usually being held. This is in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You, as a Bosnian volunteer, did not report at the Zagreb mosque to go to Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. I did not report there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Zagreb mosque did not have anything to do with your arrival as a Bosnian volunteer to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You said that you were met by the Territorial Defence in Travnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You were assigned to the front line immediately; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Before that, you did not have any military experience; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You didn't even serve the military term of duty in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, before you were assigned by the Territorial Defence to the lines, you did not go through basic training, did you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the collection centre of Bosnian volunteers in Zagreb, there wasn't a single foreign fighter with you, an Arab; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you said that you were assigned to the Krajina unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You will agree with me that at least a half of the fighters of that unit did not have weapons at all, did they?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You didn't have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had some old uniforms, but we didn't all have them. We had some old American uniforms that were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. It would be fair to conclude, wouldn't it, that this unit where you were, the Krajina Battalion, was an average unit of the Territorial Defence or the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So we could say that it was unequipped?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Regardless of everything, I would like to suggest something to you. Regardless of the difficult conditions in which it operated, we saw these refugees, Witness; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The lack of equipment. Would you agree with me that the Krajina unit still tried to introduce order and discipline amongst its fighters; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now please show the witness Exhibit 42. It's a Defence exhibit, D42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May Exhibit D42 please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the transcript, until we see the document, I'm going to say, Your Honours, that this is the code of conduct of fighters of Bosanska Krajina. Thank you very much. I would like to have the Bosnian version of the document enlarged a little bit, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, now I'm going to quote from the code. The document states: "A fighter of Bosnian Krajina, a combatant of the Bosnian Krajina is member of the single army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And it goes on to say: "I shall defend and protect." I'm not going to read everything to you, just some parts. It says: "The rights, freedoms and property of the people and citizens of the Republic." And then it goes on to say -- it mentions the rules of conduct before, during, and after combat operations. I would like you to look at paragraph 4 from the top, where it says: "I shall set a personal example and thus strengthen military discipline and contribute to the firmness and monolithic character of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina units." Then I am going to read to you paragraph 6. It says: "I shall treat prisoners and civilians in the spirit of orders and in compliance with the Geneva Convention." And then can you please look at paragraph, the fourth one from the bottom, which says: "I shall oppose all forms of negative activities." And then it also says: "I shall preserve the reputation and honour of the unit, the flag, and the Coat of Arms of the Republic." And, finally, it says: "Upon entering the unit, I, a combatant of the Bosnian Krajina, accept the Code of conduct of combatants of the Bosnian Krajina, members of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with my signature." This document is a document of Nedzad Muharem Santa, son of Muharem, and it was signed on the 2nd of April 1992. I'm going to ask you the following: Do you know Mr. Nedzad Santa?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: He's also a fighter from Krajina from Sanski Most who ended up in Travnik; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: He was also joined the Krajina Battalion that we have been talking, that we talked about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you: It is true, is it not, that the Command of the Krajina Battalion demanded that its fighters abide by this kind of code as described here?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No distinction was made on the basis of ethnic background or religion, in terms of conduct that was required?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina were to be protected?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The official flag and the coat of arms of Bosnia and Herzegovina were to be protected?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to get an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll get an exhibit number. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. Madam Vidovic, just to remind you of our guidelines, where you've made such an extensive reading of a document, you remember you said yourself yesterday, the need to enter it into evidence becomes redundant and it just over burdens the record. If you do want it admitted, could you please try to keep your reading of that document to a limit. I think that's based on the guidelines. I know we still not have adopted them, but at least that has not been objected to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will strive to read only those portions that I deem to be relevant. That is why I opted to present just the shortest of such documents, and I read just very short excerpts from it. Thank you. Yes, I will be guided by your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we give it an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 117.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, did the witness actually sign a similar declaration? And maybe I should explain. I was always trying to be polite when I put questions to the witness while either party is examining or cross-examining. I thought that the polite way of doing it is to put the question through the counsel, rather than addressing myself directly to the witness, and I will address myself directly to the witness when we have questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to admit this into evidence, and that was to be my next witness [as interpreted] for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I asked whether you knew Mr. Santa, and you said you did. And now I want to ask you: Do you recall ever signing such a document upon joining the Krajina unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document, but I can't recall whether, at the time when I did this transfer, whether I had the time to actually sign it. I can't really remember. I know that there were many things that we were supposed to do, and I know about this document, but I can't now tell you whether I signed it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you did see this type of document in the Krajina unit, did you not?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You will agree, in fact, you have agreed, that the Command of the Krajina unit demanded discipline, but it is true, is it not, that it did not have the means to implement its orders of this nature? Am I right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was the period right at the beginning of the war, when things were getting organised slowly. It just went gradually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When I mentioned the word "means," perhaps I confused a bit. I wanted to ask you whether, at that time, it was true that there was no military police set up in 1992 and early 1993 that could be deployed to prevent any violations of this code, for instance?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it probably didn't have that many forces to do that, because chaos reigned. I can't really explain this to you. Things were just beginning to get organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. People simply left the unit because it didn't have any weapons. It didn't have anything to offer, this unit, I mean?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left because there weren't any weapons around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you were not the only one. People got transferred en masse?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, many people from Krajina joined the Muslim Forces, and there was a company-strength unit there later on, perhaps even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you did not ask for anyone's permission and that you did not report to anyone when you got the transfer?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you that the reason for this was because the level of organisation in the military units was such that there were no ways and means to prevent people from doing that, would I be right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you a precise answer to this question, but I really didn't feel any need to report to anyone. I just up and left. There were no weapons. I was not the only one who did that. I was simply not thinking in those terms. I. Probably should have reported to someone, but believe me when I say that I really didn't think about that, because quite a few of us people from Krajina left and we went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But the unit itself did not have any assets to prevent that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for sure, yeah, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You said that the army was in the process of getting established?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that, after a while, some people went back to Croatia and so on. I know that this was prohibited. People were not allowed to go back from their units, but I know that quite a few people did do just that. They went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Will you agree that in 1992, in Central Bosnia, there was general chaos? I'm not exaggerating if I say that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You answered some questions yesterday about the barracks where you were, and I would like to ask you some questions. You told us that the Krajina Battalion was in the Travnik barracks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, it is true that the barracks in question at the same time housed many of the refugees and families of the fighters who had come here from the Bosnian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The barracks was huge, and many of the families were accommodated in one part of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you told us yesterday that elements of the HVO were also there?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So we have a situation where we have the Krajina fighters, the HVO fighters, and families and many refugees in the barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you will agree with me that at the time the barracks looked like an accommodation for large numbers of people, rather than a military barracks?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that there was always a crush there. Everybody was there. It was a weird situation, but I really didn't pay much attention to that. But all kinds of things happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would be fair to say, would it not, that it was not possible for the battalion command to monitor all that was going on?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know to what extent it was possible to monitor the goings on, but the refugees were there. The HVO was separate, but the Command really didn't have -- it did not impose any kind of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, yesterday, that you had seen the foreign fighters enter the barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You don't really know why they were there?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that because I wasn't really interested in that, but I do know that I saw them on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You will indicate when it's convenient.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I will, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, regarding the Arabs, I would like to ask you one question. At that time when you were there at this location that we've been discussing, the barracks, when those people went there, it is true that at that time the Arabs had provided humanitarian aid to the refugees also?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that you were unable to distinguish between humanitarian workers and Arab fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't make this distinction at all, and I didn't really give it much thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that is why you cannot claim that the persons, those Arabs who went into the barracks, that they were fighters rather than humanitarian workers?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us that, because of the disorganization in its ranks, you left the Krajina unit and joined the so-called Muslim Forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Muslim Forces had more weapons, significantly more weapons?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is right to say that those forces were not organised according to the principle of Bosnian Army that you had belonged before?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some differences.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, do you want me to stop here for the break?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Court adjourned. We'll come back at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first of all, I would like to apologise to you and the interpreters and all those present. I understood that the break was around 10.30, and this is why I would just like to apologise before we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, we were talking about the Muslim Forces before the break, and I would like to continue with that. I would like to ask you the following: Do you agree that Muslim Forces functioned as groups?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were combat groups of 20-odd people each when I joined the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And they functioned in accordance with religious principles; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The religious influence was strong; yes, like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And they were gathered around imams, the religious officials? Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several people who had completed religious schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The group that you joined was in Travnik, right, you've told us that. And I want to ask you the following: Efendi Ahmed Adilovic was one of the key people in that group, in those forces, when you joined; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you help us, if you know, his brother was Zukdija Adilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he studied the Islamic sciences in an Arab country; is that right? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to show the witness document PT1009. Your Honours, for the transcript, I would like to say that this document has two parts. The first is this page that we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at this document? Can you see that it's a document of the defence headquarters of the Zenica District of the 21st of July, 1992; and in the heading, it says that it is sent to the Main Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to Fikret Muslimovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you also see that attached to the document, another document is being forwarded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to look at page 2 of this document. This document has the heading of "The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Zenica District Defence Staff," and bears the date 21st of July, 1992. And it can be seen that it was signed by the Chief of Security, and the document bears his stamp and signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to quote two parts from this document. The document states the following: "On the 21st of July, 1992, I received the Commander of the Municipal Staff in Travnik, R.H., for an interview at his request, and he reported the following to me: That a paramilitary unit under the name 'Muslimanske Snage,' Muslim Forces, is being formed in the territory of the Municipality of Travnik. The name of the ideological leader is Zihnija. The organisation of those units is exclusively on a single ethnic and religious basis. "They recruit men from the regular armed forces formation. Soldiers are paid 50 German marks, and officers 200 German marks a month. They spread rumours among the Muslim population that they are the only ones who are protecting the Muslims, and that under no circumstances can they be protected by someone who does not pray to God or bow down." Witness, you probably haven't seen this document, but I would like to ask you something about the facts that I have read out to you. You can see the document bears the date of 21st of July 1992, and that the Travnik Staff Commander is informing about Muslim Forces being formed in the area of Travnik, and that they're being recruited among the regular armed forces. Do you agree that this fact that this man is reporting is actually true?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that only Muslims were there is true and that no one else could join. As for the rest, I am really not familiar with those things. Some I know, and some I don't know, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And can you please tell us what you do know of what is mentioned here? Is it true that --

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only Muslims were there. No other ethnic groups could join.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You told us that you joined the unit in August; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think in late August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you also said that only Muslims were there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, now I am going to ask you this: According to what you know, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina that you were in, such as the Krajina unit or other units [as interpreted] of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, were not based on ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Battalion had Croats and even a few Serbs, but it was a multi-ethnic unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The English translation says, "units or other units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were not based on ethnicity." I'm not quite sure this is what you said, and I just wanted to find out if being a Muslim, is that an ethnic characteristic or is it a religious characteristic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I keep speaking about units. I am not linking Muslim Forces with the units of Bosnia and Herzegovina; and in the translation, it is constantly saying "other units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina." I would, first, like to clarify that. I am speaking about the Muslim Forces and about units of Bosnia and Herzegovina; while in the transcript, constantly it says "other units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina." This is what it was like yesterday and this is what it is like today, and this is why I would like the transcript to reflect my questions accurately. The other thing -- well, anyway. Thank you, Your Honours, for your intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, please, let's just clarify this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute, ma'am. I'm not quite sure what you're saying answers my question. The witness has said that from this document, the one thing that he knows is correct is that only Muslims were members. My question to you is, and I just want clarity here: When you talk of "Muslims," are you talking of an ethnic group or are you talking of a religious group? And the only reason I'm asking is because the English interpretation refers to ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, when you said "Muslims," did you mean the Muslim faith or did you mean Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant were Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So Bosniaks of Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, this is a problem I have with this. It's actually a translation problem, if you will, because I see in the English version that we're talking about ethnicity; whereas, in my headphones, I hear the French and we're talking about national basis. So a national basis, or a nationality, and ethnicity are two different things. This is what I would like to know: Would it be possible for Ms. Vidovic to explain to me, or the witness, if they are talking about an ethnic, ethnicity, or are they talking about a nationality? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the best thing perhaps would be to read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or a religion?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I understand, Your Honours. The best thing would be to read the sentence of the document that I showed the witness that has to do with this part that is unclear. It says: "Only the organisation is exclusively on single ethnic and religious bases."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in relation to this, Witness, I'm going to put this question to you again so we can clarify it: Is it true that this "single ethnic" means that we are referring to only Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as for the "religious basis," that we are talking about people of the Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I am going to look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, once again, there is a discrepancy between the French version and the English version. In the English version, we're always talking about "single ethnic" and "religious bases"; whereas, in the French interpretation, and I must say I understand a little Serbian as well, and in the version that I hear from you, Ms. Vidovic, I believe you're mentioning -- or the word you're using is "nationality." You're not using the term "ethnicity"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really cannot help you there. Perhaps we can ask for an interpretation or an explanation. What is clear and what the witness has responded is that there were Bosniaks or Bosnians of the Islamic faith. This is how it was in reality. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand the Defence position. This document is submitted by the Defence. Is it the Defence's position that the Muslimanske Snage was composed exclusively of Bosniaks of Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the position, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, I see on this document that it is written that the name -- that the organisation of the unit is exclusively on a "single nation" and on "religious basis." The transcript says "ethnicity." So I would then want to understand that the position of the Defence is that the Muslimanske Snage didn't have any person who was not a Bosniak and who didn't also belong to the religion of Islam?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is how I understood the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me. Now I am getting confused, because I would have thought that the Muslimanske Snage also comprised the Arabs; that is to say, people who were not Bosnians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the purpose of this document and the question, actually, this is something that I'm just going to clarify within the next half an hour. Yes. I'm going to come to that topic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just one more thing in relation to this document. Witness, I would just like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we still have the document on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. I would just like you to look at this enclosure, insignia of Muslim Forces. So this insignia here. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, do you remember this insignia?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is this the insignia that you wore when you were in the Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, perhaps we can -- I would like to tender this document. Can it please be given an exhibit number. Can we please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm waiting for this interpretation. Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 118.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to show the witness document -- Exhibit 103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is the exhibit shown to the witness yesterday by the Prosecutor. Please, can we zoom in on the first part of this document? Can we also look at the English version? This is a list of fighters of the Muslim fighters from the area of Travnik, dated the 15th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please look at the person listed under number 2? This is Abdula Makteuf, son of Muhammad, born in 1959. The Prosecutor asked you about this person yesterday, and you said that you know who this person is?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you know that the person is from Iraq?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, please. It's true, isn't it, that that person lived in and worked in Bosnia at least ten years before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the war. I know that he was there for a long time, but I don't know for how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also probably -- you also probably know that he was married to a woman from Travnik and that he had a family there before the war?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: He also had his shop before the war that was called his shop before the war, let's say?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in some kind of business, but I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask a question. To your knowledge, do you know if this person had a Bosnian nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In this respect, Witness, I would like to ask you the following question, please: It would be wrong to conclude -- on the basis of his name on this list, it would be wrong, rather, to consider him a foreign fighter, a Mujahid, who had come to fight in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had lived there for a long time before the war, so, no, he did not come during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. So on the basis of his example, it would be wrong to conclude that the foreign fighters were members of the Muslim Forces, on the basis of his name?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, foreign fighters were not there. There were just us, and we had our records. Records were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like you to answer my question: On the basis of his example, because his name is listed here, it would be wrong to conclude that foreign fighters were members of the Muslim Forces? Did you understand what I want to say?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is your answer?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like you to look at page 2 of this document, or rather, page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the ERN number is 0129-8780.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at this sign on this document. You saw the insignia of the Muslim Forces a little while ago, and do you agree with me that this is the insignia of the Muslim Forces on the stamp?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I don't have any more questions related to this document, so we can put it away. Now I would like to ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit 116. It's the document with the patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like you to look at this document once again. I'm not talking about the insignia that you wore. I would like you to look at the patch listed under 12.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the patch worn by the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've seen a little while ago, in the document that we showed you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in fact, I forgot to ask admission for the document that we used before, the one that was numbered 103, the document that contained the insignia of the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And will you agree with me that it did not bear any insignia of the BH Army there?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any insignia of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I am going to spend some more time dealing with the Muslim Forces and the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In general, I would like to ask you once again about the situation in the field in 1992 and 1993. You agreed with me that chaos had reigned there in 1992 and the first half of 1993; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would never occur to you that the BH Army units had proper military organisation; for instance, the Krajina unit that you belonged to or any other units that you were able to observe?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, and perhaps even into 1993, things were getting organised. After the conflict with the Croats, this was when the army became well structured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question. I think that you may have information, relevant information. The situation was so chaotic among the BH Army units in this area that they would fire at each other. BH Army units in the field would fire on each other, because of this lack of organisation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which area are we specifically talking about, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about the Travnik area all the time. That's where the witness was operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I don't know if you can assist me.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I supposed to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that while I was in the barracks and when we came back from our first tour of duty in the field, there were some incidents in Travnik, two or three such incidents. I, myself, participated in such an incident. There was a clash between a local unit and some of us from Krajina, and a local member was wounded in this clash.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that this was because the army was not properly organised?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was because the situation was complex because of the chaos. I don't know. I can't really tell you why. But two or three times I was there when there would be those clashes, because there was no military police to introduce any sort of -- compose any sort of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I would now like to ask you some questions about foreign fighters. Yesterday, you gave evidence about foreign fighters, Arabs, whom you had seen in the fighting before you joined the El Mujahid Detachment, and I would like to ask you the following. I would like to ask you to do the following: Just listen to my questions, because I want to ask you questions that relate to the period before you joined the detachment and after the detachment. So my question now relates to the events that preceded the time when you became a member of the El Mujahid Detachment. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You explained to us that sometimes you had fought in the same areas with the Arab fighters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you said that you fought the same enemy?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us at that time that you were in the Muslim Forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would be wrong to say, would it not, that they were, I mean, the Arabs, were under the command of the Muslim Forces in those actions?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had those special groups. The first time that I went into action, there were two or three groups there. An Arab, a Turkish, and perhaps another group were there, and they were independent, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You said that they had their own commanders?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You had your own commanders; is that true?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You testified that you went to Karaula and that you found the Arabs there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You fought up there for a while; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does the name Faruk Selman mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do recognise the name. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm talking about Faruk Selman, born in 1973, from Kljaci. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know two brothers. One is Faruk and the other might be Fijic. One of them was killed. I can't now remember which was which. But at any rate, there were two brothers, and one of them was Faruk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you're sure that one of them -- one of them got killed at Karaula?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence yesterday, you mentioned Abu Ubeidah?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met him at Karaula.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If someone were to say that his group fought under the command of the Muslim Forces, that would not be true; is that so?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had their own weapons, their own logistics, so they were there as independent operators. Abu Ubeidah was one of them. I met two of them. I don't remember the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will go back to this question later. But I would like you to assist the Trial Chamber, and all of us, indeed, to understand how the Arab forces operated in the field in Central Bosnia. You will agree with me, will you not, that in Central Bosnia, throughout the war, there were several different groups of foreign fighters active in that area?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a few of those Arab groups. There were the Arabs at Karaula, some at Mehurici. There were some at -- in Tesanj and in some other towns. I know that there were quite a few of them. I don't know some of those groups, but I know that there were many of them, and I have heard about some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine, fine. I will take this slowly. They operated in 1992 and 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout the war, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In 1995, too, they took part in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And they included in their ranks Turks, Arabs, Iraqis, Algerians, Libyans, Saudi Arabians?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from many Arab countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us that Abu Ubeidah's group was not the only group of foreigners that was there while you were at Karaula?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the only one, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is true that there was a group of Turks operating independently from him? I don't know if you know about that.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were a separate unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They had their own emir; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They did, but I don't remember his name. I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. In your evidence yesterday, in answer to the questions the Judges put to you about the coordination between Arabs and the Muslim Forces in Bijelo Bucje, do you remember that? You answered those questions, and let me just remind you. At page 52 of the transcript, lines 10 through 13, you said -- you said, "There were very frequent attacks and actions, with run-around in all directions. There were constant attacks. We had light weapons, and we were attacked by tanks." On the basis of what you said, Witness, I conclude that there was no coordination. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was among the most difficult situations I found myself in during the war. I can't really see any coordination there, because we went to the confrontation lines all day. We were there all day and all the nights, and I really can't see any coordination because attacks -- there were attacks coming on from all the sides. So I can't really see how anything could be coordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will now move on to a different topic, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 104.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document, and I would like you to look at this page. You said yesterday, when you were asked about this document, that you find it strange; is that so?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like you to look at it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to scroll down this document a little bit so that we can -- scroll up so that we can see the heading on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is a series of names here and that somebody simply wrote, by hand, "Muslim Forces." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, could you look --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like the witness to see the entire page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree that there is nothing in this document that would indicate that the document was sent to someone?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see anything like that on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Also, you cannot see if anyone received this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing, other than names, on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as I understood from what you said, you lived your whole life in Bosnia and Herzegovina. If I were to say to you that you did not read in any document in your life that it says "Mithat ibn Ismet" or "Ahmet ibn" something. Would I be right? This is not something that's customary, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've absolutely never seen anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, Your Honours, I would like the witness to look at page 06032514 of this document, 06032514. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the document? Do you agree that the typing, the typewritten text finishes at number 89?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then you can see that from 91 to 97, a number of Arab names was written by hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I carefully followed your testimony yesterday. You looked at different lists. You did not identify any of these persons with these names as members of the detachment; is that correct? Please, can you look at these names?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names are not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: None of the persons here -- I asked you now about members of the detachment, but would you say that any of these persons were people that you met while you were in the Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names are not familiar to me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you cannot confirm if any of them was a member of the Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to put some questions to you about the 7th Muslim Brigade. You became a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade when it was established?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you yesterday Exhibit 107.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to see the document, again, please. For the transcript, Your Honours, I would just like to say that this is a document of the Armed Forces, Supreme Command Staff, of the 19th of November 1992, to the 3rd Corps Command. The Chief of Staff is the signature. Your Honours, I would ask the witness to do the same thing the Prosecutor asked him to do yesterday, and that is to look at paragraph number 1 that says "Formation." The document says: "I order organisational preparations, formation. Form a mountain brigade under the name of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade from the ARBiH armed units currently engaged on the Vlasic plateau. Form the brigade in accordance with the temporary wartime establishment," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, this document orders that the 7th Muslim Brigade be formed from forces engaged on the Vlasic plateau; and in relation to that, I would like to put the following question to you: You also fought at the Vlasic plateau; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would be wrong now, wouldn't it, to believe that only Muslim Forces exclusively were at the Vlasic plateau? That would be wrong to believe?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Vlasic plateau was full of different units. It's a large area, and there were different units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us this yesterday, but I would like to clarify the following with you now. I assert that the brigade comprised at least four groups of fighters. I'm going to ask you about each one separately, and I would like you to answer with a "yes" or "no" to my question. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The first group were members of the army of the Travnik Territorial Defence Municipal Staff; am I right, if you know, of course?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The first group that fought on the Vlasic plateau was that of the members of the Municipal Staff of the Travnik Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The second group was members of other units of the armija; for example, the 308th and the 312th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what their names were, but I know that there was a brigade from Novi Travnik and a brigade from Travnik. It's possible that it was the 312th. I'm not sure right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, that is an answer to my question. Thank you. And then there was this group that you fought in, the members of the Muslimanske Snage from Travnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, finally, there was a group of able-bodied men who had not fought anywhere before that; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you now about all of this is the following: It would be wrong, wouldn't it, to claim that all members of the Muslim Forces, the Muslimanske Snage, were automatically part of the 7th Muslim Brigade or the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this was. I was out in the field a lot. I know that there was a reorganisation underway. So who was part of that, specifically, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Am I right when I think that some of your co-fighters crossed into the 308th or into the 312th or, let's say, these Travnik brigades that you mentioned earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look. People frequently switched from one unit to another, so this is possible. There were lots of people moving from one brigade to another, one unit to another. The units changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But it is also right that some of your co-fighters immediately joined the Arabs and did not join the 7th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is possible. I don't know. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. In any case, you said that you became a member of the 7th Muslim at the end of 1992, and I would now like to ask you something about the 7th Brigade itself, about how it was structured, please. It's right, isn't it, that the 7th Muslim, at the point in time when you joined it, did not look like an ordered military unit, a structured military unit; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that. The reorganisation and the structuring took place only after the conflicts with the HVO were over. That was when some sort of a system was set up in the 7th, in the Krajina, and in all the other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the winter of 1992 until the summer of 1993, because now you have limited us to that period, I would be right if I believe that the 7th Muslim did not have a professional military command, wouldn't I?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a command, but it was these emirs. It was this religious influence there. And as for how all of that looked, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The gist of my question is the following: It did not have a militarily-educated staff or personnel. When I say that, I mean officers who had completed military academies. That is the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. Perhaps some did have something, but these were not military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The first commander, Mr. Asim Koricic, was a sportsman, an athlete, and he completed sports trainer education; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is more or less what I heard, and I think that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So he did not complete military academy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to show the witness document D47. This is a Defence exhibit. Your Honours, that is not that number, but we can do it like this.
