Can we show the witness, please, document ERN 0181-1276. Your Honours, the e-court is showing D46, but this is -- we need document 0181-1276. Thank you very much. We found the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. This is a document of the Commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim, Fadil Hodzic, and you can see in the upper corner that the document was drafted on the 15th of March 1993. Witness, now you can see the date of the document, and I can see, Witness, that you are tired, but I'm going to read two small -- I'm going to quote two small parts of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please just -- all right. And maybe the Bosnian version, we can zoom in a little bit on it so the witness can see it a little better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And before we begin to quote from the document, I would like to ask you if you knew Mr. Fadil Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to quote a small part of the document, which says, this is the first part of the first paragraph of the document: "Because of his improper behaviour and failure to carry out orders issued by the Commander of the 1st Battalion that he refused to carry out, I demand that the company commander, Redzo Kavazovic, be taken to task and punished." And then lower the document goes on to say, in the time period, from the 12th to the 18th of February, 1993, he refused to return to his unit, ignoring all calls by the Commander of the 1st battalion, and summoned 20 soldiers who supported him. And then after that, it says, in one case, he publicly told the soldiers that he could drink a beer and that that was no shame at all. I have one question about this. Did you know Redzo Kavazovic?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the last name, but it's possible that it's Redzo from the Vitez Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Redzo from Vitez. He -- I don't know his last name, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that the Travnik MOS became the 1st Battalion of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that it transformed, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I want to ask you this on that topic: If I were to suggest to you that there were other fighters in that battalion who were not members of the Muslimanske Snage, like this Redzo, would I be right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that later people from Vitez joined this battalion. I knew Redzo from Vitez also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. This document indicates that fighters within the battalion of the 7th had conflicts because of different attitudes in terms of accepting religious precepts about behaviour in the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some people. Some people did not wish to adhere to certain things, and occasionally there was the odd incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, it seems that this Redzo thought it was a normal thing for him to drink beer?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was a bit more free in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, according to the document, he did not observe orders by the commander?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was a specific sort of person. That's how I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you is the following: This document actually reflects the actual situation in the battalion, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. How can I put it? There were different people with different personal attitudes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When I was reading the document, and you can see that on the screen - we don't want to lose too much time here - the document refers to Efendi Adilovic in several place. You said that he was the Travnik imam; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you know that he was the director of the Travnik medresa during the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an emir, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. You said that he was an emir. What I would like to ask you is the following: It seems that his influence was quite strong, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was practically the religious leader, and his influence was quite strong in the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Based on this document, when you read it, you would say that Efendi Adilovic mediated in conflicts there. Would you please agree that I am right if I, on the basis of this document, conclude that the battalion, the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim, in the first months of its existence there was confusion? Would that be the correct conclusion?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it included people from Vitez, and there were a couple of groups, companies there. People had different positions. Emir Ahmed Adilovic was there, authorised to tell people what they should do, what they had to do in such-and-such a case, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You saw that this document that we have just put away bore the date of the 15th of March. It was signed by Fadil Hodzic? What I would like you to look at now is another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can you show document D44, Exhibit D44, to the witness, and you will see the document and that it bears the date of the 13th of March, 1993. Your Honours, for the transcript, this is a document from the Command of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the 13th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the end of the document, it says: "Commander of the 1st battalion, Ahmet Zubaca." Witness, can you please look at the second page of the document, which bears the number 0181-1282. It says: "As for the equipment, problems are cropping up. The uniforms are old and tore." You've already told us that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show page 1 of this document to the witness, 0181-1281.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just quote a very small portion of this document to you. It says here the command and control system, because of the lack of expertise and training among the personnel, is not functioning as it should be. Apart from lack of expertise and training, the command and control system is also impaired by the manifest bypassing of some command levels, both from below upwards and vice versa. Also, the command and control system is adversely affected by the fact that the battalion has not been fully structured yet. I would now like to point your attention to paragraph 4, where it says that the improper and inadequate record-keeping causes problems in this respect. The unit and personnel records have not been done yet because of the shortage of forms. There aren't enough forms. You belonged to this battalion in the 7th Muslim Brigade. You will agree with me that this document reflects the actual situation on the 13th of March, or rather, in that time period, in the spring, in this battalion of the 7th Muslim that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The command system in the battalion did not function, lack of expertise in control?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how it functioned, but what I do know is that structure was not in place at that time. Let me repeat, once again. Once the conflict with the Croats was over, everything was set up as it should be. Up until that time, everything was very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you just one more question in this regard. The document talks about improper and inadequate record-keeping, and it is stated that there were no personnel record forms. Is that something you knew about?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nothing was done as it should have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this would be an appropriate time for the break, but if we could just get an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document D44 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And, then, that will be an appropriate time to take a break. Court adjourned and we'll come back at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, before the break, we were talking about command and control in the spring of 1993, and you explained to us how it functioned all the way up to the time when the conflict with the Croat forces ended in that area. You agreed that the command and control in the 1st Battalion was bad in the end of March 1993, and I want to ask you this: You will agree with me that the situation right at the start, at the end of 1992, could only have been worse?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In your evidence yesterday, you mentioned Ramo Durmis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us that he liked to be called "Abu Jihad"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You will agree with me that several persons, both among Arabs and locals, had that nickname, "Abu Jihad"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some Arabs that used that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And our local Muslims also liked to use such shortened names?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I had a nickname, too. It was a little bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ramo Durmis was not the only Muslim who had that nickname, "Abu Jihad"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us that he joined the 7th Muslim Brigade, the 1st Battalion, when it was established; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you did, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: He was the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion in December of 1992. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander. I don't know in what period, but it's possible that he was the commander in December. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine. He was a member of Muslimanske Snage before, just like you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was, but I don't know when he joined. But he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you will agree with me that the members of Muslimanske Snage, the Muslim Forces, were reluctant - now we're talking about the very beginning of the functioning of the 7th Muslim Brigade - were not so very happy with accepting the BH Army units because of their diverse ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I want to say the following: Members of Muslimanske Snage were not all that happy to be members of the BH Army that was not composed only of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a preference for Muslims; yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In fact, to make things clearer, they did not consider it to be a Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Because you told us that's what it was not; it contained people of other ethnic backgrounds?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the beginning, they were suspicious of the members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They even feared that they would betray them sometimes?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I may be allowed to explain. I know that when Major Tara came to the Muslimanske Snage, he was an active-duty serviceman, and we didn't really trust him because he was from the army, because the people were saying that he was there to tear the Muslimanske Snage apart, to destroy them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, they had those reservations vis-a-vis the BH Army, because it accepted into its ranks members of the former Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA, because the JNA was considered to have been a Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They considered Communists to be infidels?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They called them "cafalic kafar" [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would be devils. This term means "devils"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to show a document to this witness. It is PT1024. Your Honours, I would like you to -- I would like to ask you for some indulgence on your part. I believe that it would assist the Chamber and all of us to get the interpretation from this witness about some passages, and I will be therefore reading a longer excerpt. But I will try to keep it as short as possible and not to overdo it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I don't know if you can see this document here. The title of this document is "The Report on the Operations of the 1st Company in the Visoko-Buci-Rakovci-Visegrad Elevation Sector." The way I understood your evidence yesterday -- perhaps I misunderstood you. Did I understand you correctly that you knew something about the participation of Arabs at this operation in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know they participated in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to quote from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a document, we will see at the end that it is signed by the commander of the 1st Company, Ramo Durmis, and it says as follows: "The action was carried out on the 28th of December, 1992, at 0600 hours. Following Terzic's orders, issued over the telephone, I suddenly became a member of the team that was supposed to go to Visoko. Under the agreement in the command, we were supposed to leave on the morning of the 25th of December, but it was delayed 'til evening and we had to wait for the equipment. "We had a brief meeting in the command in a school in Zenica, at which I said to Comrade Patkovic, in unequivocal terms, and warned him not to rely too much on the army, members of the Territorial Defence (the overall number of troops, fire support, and logistics). "Serif Patkovic gave me a perfect answer: 'Our task is to capture certain elevations; but if the Territorial Defence betrays us, we will bring the Mujahids back to reserve positions.'. "Since I became involved in this action suddenly, I became slightly worried about the level of equipment of the Mujahedin, and immediately the Muslim Forces in Zenica gave me a warm welcome when I tried to exchange some boots." And just one more excerpt, where it says: "We all heard our tasks, and I again pointed out to Patkovic, in the name of Allah, that the TO should not betray us right at the right side, and he replied to me that this would be an easy job for them."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you as follows. Let's just clear this up for the Chamber, so that they know what we're talking about. You told us that the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade was Asim Koricic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Serif Patkovic was the commander of the 2nd Battalion in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I can't remember, but I know that he was one of the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if I were to say that, at that time, Terzic was an operations officer in the brigade command, would I be right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ramo Durmis, the commander of the 1st Company, describing this action of the 28th of December, 1992, says: "In a school in Zenica, I told Patkovic, I said to Patkovic not to count too much on the army, fearing the betrayal on the part of the Territorial Defence." And in this respect, I would like to ask you: It is true, is it not, that throughout 1992, members of the Bosnian Army were called the Territorial Defence or just "the army"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would appear from this document that Durmis does not consider himself to be a member of the Bosnian Army; although, he was in the 7th Muslim Brigade. It was a brigade that was part of the army. Would you draw this conclusion on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really make any claims, but I do know that we always suspected that there might be betrayal because there were Serbs and Croats in the ranks, and there was definitely some mistrust. I can't really tell you about how he felt at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. It's a fair-enough answer. I want to ask you the following: It is quite clear that this document shows that the author, to say the least, made the distinction between himself and his group and the Territorial Defence; would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this despite the fact that formally [Realtime transcript read in error "formerly"] they were members of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, it is true that this document reflects the situation in the field when it comes to these facts?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, just a matter of precision. In fact, I only see the witness nodding his head, and I suppose this means "yes." But for the record, perhaps, we should ensure that you do not assume any positive answers which are not clearly expressed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we are on that, may I just ask: You said, "And this despite the fact that formally they were members of the 7th Brigade." By "formally" did you mean "in form," or did you mean "before"? Because it's written there "formerly," meaning "before. " That's line 21. And I would imagine that you meant to say "in form, they were members of the ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. In Bosnian, I said "formally." You're right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it has got to be f-o-r-m-a-l-l-y, not m-e-r?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, "formally." That's right. That they were "formally," not "formerly." Yes. I was very clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, His Honour Judge Harhoff asked you to say "yes." In response to my previous question, did you answer "yes"? Actually, you just nodded, so your answer was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to read a part of the document to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please can the witness be shown page 01832730, or the second page of this document. I'm going to read a small part of the document, which states -- I am reading from the third section, which begins with: "Some Mujahid ..." I'm reading from the third section: "Some Mujahids, including Arabs, moved towards Elevation 744 to the right without my order; then they came down to the village and started torching. I caught up with two Mujahids and informed Emir Heldic [phoen] that he and the Mujahids must withdraw. However, the Arabs went even further to the right. Emir Heldic and his group returned before midday; but Abu Talha [phoen], deceased, with the Arabs and the Turks, remained in the depth on the right side."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you already told us that -- you told us that Arabs also took part in this battle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Arabs and Turks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, please, you could conclude that they were at the Visegrad elevation in this battle with Ramo Durmis, because it says the Mujahids went, including some Arabs; was that how it was?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that was how it actually was, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there. It's just that they wanted to go somewhere independently. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you this: Do you consider, first of all, that this part of the report is correct? Let me put it to you line this. This document says -- or the author, Ramo Durmis, says: "Arabs without my command set off. I ordered them to withdraw, while they actually went even further into the depths." So I want to ask you the following: It's a fact that neither Abu Talha nor the Arabs or Turks listened to the commands of Ramo Durmis; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall that event. Because of it, we had vast casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thus, the Arabs had their own ways of fighting, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The document, on its face, indicates, and I'm quoting: "Some Mujahids, including Arabs." And the questions coming from my learned colleague seems to be focusing exclusively on Arabs; whereas, the document may be referring to something other than just the Arabs, and I would ask that believe clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As you clarify that, could you also clarify the fact that document doesn't say "all Mujahids," but some of them, and some of them may have stayed with the troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, Witness, the document says that "some Mujahids, including Arabs." First of all, let me ask you, it's correct, isn't it, that there were Bosniaks together with the Arabs already, that some who did not join the 7th from the MOS already then had gone and joined the Arabs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but I'm not sure about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right, very well. It says: "Mujahids, including Arabs, without my order." Do you agree -- how would you understand that? You were there in the field, so I want to ask you, please: At the time, in the field, did Arabs listen to the Bosnian command, whether it came from the Bosnian forces or anyone else's command?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me explain. I personally was at that elevation, and the order was that when we captured it, we would wait there until other units came. However, the Arabs went into the depth several kilometres, four to five kilometres into the depth, without waiting. They didn't wish to wait there. I don't know what their reasons were. All of us stayed there, as far as us Bosniaks were concerned because later, because of their -- the fact that they had gone down there, we were not able to hold it by ourselves. We had enormous casualties. The Arabs also had casualties. Many of them were killed, too, because they left.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Witness. Thank you very much. Could this document be tendered as an exhibit and given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, please, if I were to say that it was precisely this event at the Visegrad elevation was very important for future relations between Arabs and Bosnians, would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some things became very different after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will come to that, that they became different,, Witness. Witness, could you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we returned from the action, we had vast casualties. Perhaps 40 to 50 people were killed. Over 100 were wounded. They blamed the officers of the BiH Army, that they had pushed us to death deliberately, and then they turned even more in the sense that absolutely there was no more respect towards the officers and towards the commands. And it was even likely that serious consequences could occur. There was even an incident and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to say something which I forgot to say when we came back from the break. It came to the notice of the Chamber during the break that the witness complained of a headache, and I just wanted to say to him that if and when he does feel tired and he feels he needs a break, he must please indicate. First of all, are you able to carry on, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But when you feel tired or maybe you feel your headache is severe and you need a break, please to indicate. Thank you. You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, before you move on, I didn't quite understand the testimony of the witness when he said that they were complaining when they came home to the BiH command, as I understood, complaining towards their leaders about the fate that had arrived to them that same day. If I understand correctly, the Muslim Forces were sent out to occupy the Visegrad elevation; and when they had done that, they were told to wait. Some of them waited, but the Arabs proceeded and disappeared. And because they were then fewer in numbers, they were, at some later point, attacked by the enemy and thereby suffered great losses, and they had to retreat. And when they came back, they complained to the leaders. But did they -- what was the allegation that was made to the leaders? They should have blamed the Arabs, shouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems -- I don't know what the matter is. It seems that -- well, actually, the most important part of the witness's answer was perhaps noted and is perhaps not in the transcript, and that is that the witness specifically said that Arabs did not listen to the command to -- they did not listen. And that actually disregarding the order they went into action, and they did not listen and did not come back, and that is why there were consequences. And about the second part of your question, I'm going to now clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, Witness, when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just understand clearly, too. You're saying the witness said that Arabs did not listen to orders. Is the witness, therefore, departing from the document? Because the document doesn't say the Arabs, the document says "some Mujahids, including Arabs." So one would expect that this group that went off and didn't take orders would have been a group of Mujahids, which composed of a mixture of Bosniaks and foreigners. Now, he is now saying the Arabs only, so the Bosniaks -- is the contention that only Arabs moved away, or is he confirming this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, please, I believe that you understood the question. Is it correct that this group of Arabs, including Mujahids that were with them, did not listen to the order and went there?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not a group of Arabs. It's a group of Mujahids that included Arabs, according to the document. Unfortunately, the document is not on the screen any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the witness is giving very clear answers, and I believe that it is very clear that Arabs did not observe, and the Mujahids that were with them in the group. And I believe that that is precisely what it says in the document. I really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is not what it says in the document, madam. If you put the English part up, I'll tell you. Let's just read it. It says: "Some Mujahids, including Arabs," not Arabs, including Mujahids. The document says: "Some Mujahids, including Arabs, moved to Elevation 734." Now, what I am asking you is: Is the witness saying this document is wrong? It is not "some Arabs, including Mujahids." It is all the Arabs, including some Mujahids? That's all I want to find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, could you clarify this, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that all the Arabs left; the Turks and some of the Bosniaks also. I don't know. As for the Arabs and the Turks, I know all of them left without the order. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I was just going to suggest perhaps if the witness knows, if he could tell us what the term "Mujahid" means, which might help clarify the situation. It's just a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can you please clarify that, what the term "Mujahid" means?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "Mujahid" means the person or he who fights in the name of Allah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I'm now going to go back to Ramo Durmis. It's correct, isn't it, that Ramo Durmis, after this incident, was in conflict with the command of the units in Visoko; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an armed incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So it was a physical conflict?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physical, with weapons, everything, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you tell the Chamber, who did Ramo Durmis and the group with him attack at that time?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot definitely say by names. I know that they left and they went to the command in Visoko, where there were senior officers. They went with weapons. He went. There were a couple of Bosniaks with him and a couple of Arabs or Turks; a few foreigners and a few Bosniaks, in any case. They went to the command. They began to fight some people. They began to beat some people, and then they used their weapons. They fired everywhere. I don't know. I don't know. I don't think that anyone was actually killed, but it was quite an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that after this incident, there was a conflict within the 7th Muslim with Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were problems that dragged out then, because he should not have done that. He shouldn't have done it. If there were any problems in the course of an action, he should have discussed what happened; whereas, he went and created a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. And, finally, it's correct, isn't it, that Ramo Durmis, in late January 1993, left the 7th Muslim. He left the 7th Muslim Brigade; do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the time period when he left. All I know is that after that, he disappeared somewhere. I don't know. We were in Travnik. He was actually from Zenica, and I didn't see him in Travnik anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The witness's testimony brings me back to the question that I put to you, through you to the witness just a while ago. I still do not understand. What was the issue at that incident? And to be precise about what I'm asking, was the Command of the Muslim Brigade criticised for having dispatched this force into the field in a mission in which they knew that the Arabs, or perhaps somebody else,, would not follow orders and thereby bring the whole operation into danger? Was that the criticism that was put to the leadership?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, did you understand the question? I would like to ask you -- I have to apologise. It slipped my mind, and it was my intention to ask this question. When you said that they complained, what did you mean when you said that, that they complained? Who did they complain to? Did they talk about it amongst themselves?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the end of the action, there was a discussion among them, and they decided that it was not all the fault of the Arabs who had gone there on their own initiative, but that it was also the fault of the BH Army because they had not sent us any assistance. So Arabs were to blame, but the BH Army officers were also to blame, even -- perhaps even more so, because they should have sent assistance to us, to that line. And that is why people were more angry at the BH Army command in Visoko than the Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In other words, you did not complain to the BH Army command about that, but you discussed this among yourselves?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We discussed this amongst ourselves, and then Ramo went with some people. He picked up some Bosniaks and some Arabs, and he went there to try and get his justice done.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, I thought that you would have some more questions. Now I would like the witness to see a new document. It's D96, and the number is 0180-4491. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This is a document originating from the 7th Muslim Brigade. The date is the 19th of February, 1993. Witness, I would like to ask you to look at this document. It is a form that has been filled in. This would be the command personnel in the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I would like to have you look at this. First of all, I want to ask you whether you agree with me that this document bears the date of the 19th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we perhaps zoom it in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 19th of February, 1993, yes?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at those names? You told us that you knew Fadil Hodzic; and in particular, I want to point out to you the last four names. This is in light of the time, the date. Do you agree that this lists the commanders of companies in the 1st Battalion? I would like you to look at those names first.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know most of these people; I know Muhammad; I know Fuad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And it is true that at that time the commander of the 1st Battalion was Fadil Hodzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when he was the commander. I do know that he was, but I don't know the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine. Could you please look at the commander of 1st Company, Muhamed Basic, father's name Mustafa?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it true that he was the company commander in that period of time? Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a commander for a while, but I don't know the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine. Could you perhaps remember approximately the time period when he was the commander?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that it was in 1993, but I really can't be more specific than that. I know that he was a commander for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you very much. If this document suggests that Muhamed Basic was the commander of the 1st Company, that means that Ramo Durmis could not be the commander at that time anymore? Or to rephrase the question: In mid-February 1993, Ramo Durmis was no longer the commander of the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left somewhere after this action. He didn't come to Travnik anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I would like to ask for this document to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, in fact, Ramo Durmis is not the only person to have left the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade at that time; is that not the case?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite a few people left after this action. People left left. Some of them had been commanders. Quite a few people left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us a little while ago that, after this incident, the relations between the 7th and the Arabs in the field got more tense?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it true that these problems, at one point, culminated with the physical clash in the command of the 7th Brigade sometime in the spring of 1993? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know about this incident at Zenica, at the Command, when two Arabs were killed by members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So two Arabs were killed at the Command of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, I would like the witness to have a look at Exhibit 108. It was shown to him yesterday by the Prosecution, and the ERN number is 0181-4777.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I hope you remember that the Prosecutor showed you this document yesterday, and we asked you about Item 1(a), (b). And in Item (b), it says that additionally there are around 60 Arabs and Turks who also are not included in this total. Do you agree with me that this document, the way it is stated here, is quite unclear?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday that I didn't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me now ask you some questions about Asim Koricic. You said that he was not a trained military officer?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The battalion did not have military officers who would know how to write a clear and proper report at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people would write it any way they saw fit. The only thing that was important is to have paperwork, but there were no people who were experts in that, who specialised in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you, Witness, in the spring of 1993, you were in this battalion. If I were to put it to you that at that time, in March 1993, the 15th of March, 1993, that there were no Mujahedin in the 1st Battalion, or foreign fighters, am I right? Would I be right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that there were any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And it is true that in the spring of 1993, once Ramo Durmis had left, and even before that, but once Ramo Durmis and the group left, that the ties between the Mujahedin and the 7th Muslim Brigade were cut?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the situation changed quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Now I have a question to you, actually, because you seem to be equating Mujahedin with foreign fighters. I'm willing to go along with it. But I think that when we asked the witness just a while ago about how the term "Mujahedin" was to be understood, he answered that "Mujahedin" is everyone who fights in the name of Allah.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, am I right when I say that the Mujahedin in the field, at the time that we're talking about now, as a concept, included foreign fighters and locals who had joined them and dressed and behaved in the same manner as they did? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This term included all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess, Madam Vidovic, what prompted Judge Harhoff's question is the fact that at page 51, I think starting from line 12, you said: "I want to ask you, Witness, in the spring of 1993, you were in this battalion. If I were to put it to you that at that time in March 1993, the 15th of March, 1993, that there were no Mujahedin in the 1st Battalion or foreign fighters, would I be right?" I guess the question from the Judge is: Are you talking about Mujahedin or are you talking about foreign fighters?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you very much for this intervention. I would like to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, did you understand my question to refer to the foreign fighters and the local Mujahedin, such as Ramo Durmis and others; is that the way you understood me?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way I understood you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Therefore, the answer is that by the 15th of March, 1993, the 1st Battalion did not include any Mujahedin, be he local or foreigner?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is true, Witness, is it not?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those terms were not used at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. The terms may not have been used at that time, but what was the fact, insofar as you knew the facts on the ground, at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't really assist you all that much here, because we didn't have that much contact with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But what then is your answer to the question put to you by counsel for the Defence? On the 13th of March, 1993, what was the 1st Battalion composed of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm really confused now. These three or four questions that are now being put to me, I really can't find my way around them at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've noticed that the witness is holding his head, and I will try -- he seems to be upset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just about to ask the witness if he needed a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Your Honour, I would suggest that perhaps we might adjourn, or perhaps to finish, or to check with the witness. I might revisit this issue tomorrow or perhaps just to finish,, because it is my impression that the witness is really in a bad shape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to take a break at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have a headache.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do have a headache. Maybe we should take a break. Would you like a break or would you like to take time off for the rest of the day and come back tomorrow, sir? We still have 20 minutes before we knock off, but we could give you five or ten minutes' break if you think that would be fine, or otherwise we could knock off for the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whichever way you prefer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have that many questions left for the witness tomorrow. I promise that I will revisit all those issues to clarify this matter, but I think that perhaps it would be better, because even before the break I noticed that the witness could hardly sit. I don't see any reason why we should really torture him now, because I won't be asking him that many questions. I believe that I will be finished by the first break tomorrow. I don't know if the Prosecution is agreeable and, of course, the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just find out what Mr. Mundis has to say. I saw he was standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think the question has actually been answered. I was just going to get an indication of how much more time Ms. Vidovic needed for the purposes of arranging for following witnesses, what time they should be brought here. But if she thinks she would be finished by the first break, that answers my question, and we will certainly have witnesses available at that time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I suggest we adjourn for the today now and that we reconvene in Courtroom II tomorrow at 9.00 a.m. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24
